priceSnapshot.note: 77,540.6 against a rolling 24h open of 77,423.1, so plus 0.15 percent on the tape - a number that tells you almost nothing about what actually happened. Since morning marked 76,991.0 at 07:11 COT, price is 549.6 points higher, plus 0.71 percent, but it travelled 3,895.3 points to get there. The August CPI print at 07:30 COT knocked BTC to 76,001.0 inside twenty minutes, then bought it back to 79,896.3 by 09:00 COT - plus 5.12 percent off the low in under two hours - and the entire advance has since been given back. Spot now sits 2,355.7 points under the high and 1,539.6 points over the low, almost exactly mid-range. The day's UTC candle is an outside bar: open 76,574.2, high 79,896.3, low 76,001.0, a 5.09 percent range with a long wick at BOTH ends. Both sides were offered and both were rejected. Session range since the morning mark: 76,001.0 to 79,896.3.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 77,176.4, the daily EMA20, 364.2 points under spot. This is the pivot the entire add case rests on: morning published price 5.0 points UNDER this average and the whole overnight thesis was built on losing it; the CPI candle reclaimed it and it has held every hourly close since. Losing it on a settled close after an outside-day reclaim means the reclaim was itself the liquidity event, and the next measured reference below is 76,750.0 - morning's own reduce gate, which today's flush blew through by 749 points intraday without ever settling beneath it, so treat that shelf as damaged rather than supportive.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 78,066.5, the 16:00Z hourly high and the last level the fade broke, 525.9 points over spot. It is deliberately set above the 4H EMA20 at 77,887.0 rather than at it: the 1H EMA20 at 77,631.7 and the 15m EMA100 at 77,566.5 are both within 91 points of spot and would fire on any single candle of chop, and this desk's logged failure mode is acting on gates that fire on wicks. Reclaiming 78,066.5 on a settled close puts price back through the 4H EMA20 and re-opens 78,847.6 and then the 79,896.3 spike high.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from HOLD to ADD, the first non-hold stance from this session in three days, and it moves on evidence rather than impatience. Morning's 77,498.8 add gate FIRED at the 12:00Z hourly close of 78,025.1 and has stayed fired - all five settled hourly closes since are above it. The daily EMA20 at 77,176.4 was reclaimed on the same candle and has held. Open interest is down 4.22 percent from midnight to 2,147,783,589 USD and the long/short account ratio has bled from 1.61 to 1.50, so the crowding that produced two flushes in twenty-four hours is genuinely lighter. Against that: the 79,896.3 spike was rejected in full, spot is now under every 15m, 1H and 4H moving average, US 10-year yield printed a new 52-week high at 4.953 percent and traders are pricing a Fed HIKE at Wednesday's FOMC. That mix justifies a small spot tranche near a reclaimed pivot, not leverage and not a full deployment. The stop stays OFF: the next report is roughly 6.7 hours away, spot sits 1,539.6 points above the invalidation, and a resting stop that far out would only be hit by a move this report would have time to see.

Measured fills, not a forward heatmap: this marks where leverage has ALREADY been taken out, so the fuel in this band is spent - the value is that it tells you price is sitting directly on top of the densest recent unwind.

60,802 USD in the 77,850-77,949 band, 359.4 points over spot, straddling the 4H EMA20 at 77,887.0. The confluence is the point: a squeeze band and a moving average in the same 100-point pocket is what makes 78,066.5 the honest add trigger rather than 77,887.0.

liquidityMagnet.note: Both magnets sit within 260 points of spot, so as DISTANCE they are noise; the content is composition. 381,956 USD of the 532,001 USD window was LONG-side (71.8 percent) and it is stacked entirely BELOW price, which is why pull reads down. The honest caveat is the same one this desk has repeated all week: these are REALIZED fills, not resting orders. The 71.8 percent long-side skew describes the fade from 79,896.3 that has already happened, not a queue of stops waiting below. What it does establish is that the 77,300-77,500 pocket has just been cleared of leveraged longs, so if price goes back there it arrives with less to burn and less to bounce off.

calibration.rollingRecord: Morning goes 1-for-2 on gates, and the one that fired has gone from right to roughly wrong inside five hours. The 77,498.8 add gate FIRED at the 12:00Z hourly close of 78,025.1, twenty minutes after the CPI print, and every settled close since is above it - 79,251.4, 78,796.8, 77,727.0, 77,913.4 - so it never un-fired. Acting on it at the trigger close would have bought at 78,025.1; spot is 77,540.6, which is 484.5 points and 0.62 percent offside. At the 79,896.3 high that same fill was 1,871.2 points in profit, so the gate was not wrong, the exit was never written. The 76,750.0 reduce gate did NOT fire on its own terms - the lowest settled hourly close since the mark was 77,727.0, 977.0 points clear - yet price traded 749.0 points THROUGH the level intraday on the CPI candle, printing 76,001.0. That is the second time this week a settled-close gate has protected the book from a wick it would have been stopped out on, and the fifth time in six sessions that declining the resting stop was correct: morning switched the stop OFF at 76,261.0 and the low of 76,001.0 would have filled it 260 points into a move that fully reversed within ninety minutes. Discretionary: morning HELD, and holding was worth plus 549.6 points on spot against the mark. Across the last fourteen logged sessions a published gate fired in eight.
calibration.note: The lesson this session owes the log is about exits, not entries. Morning's add gate was analytically correct - it identified 77,498.8 as the level whose reclaim would mean the fade was over, and price reclaimed it and ran 1,871 points. What no report on this desk has ever published is where that trade comes OFF. Today's report answers it for the first time: the position leg carries take-profits at 78,847.6 and 79,896.3 rather than an open-ended hold.
